dedupe_keys.name: iea energy and ai data centre electricity demand estimates and projections

description: The International Energy Agency's Energy and AI work, first published in April 2025 and followed by updates such as Key Questions on Energy and AI, estimates the electricity used by data centres worldwide and by region and projects it under several cases. It rests on a new global model and dataset of data-centre electricity demand built from server shipments, data-centre capacity and project pipelines, and it separates AI-focused data centres; it reports that data-centre electricity use rose about 17 percent in 2025 and projects roughly a doubling to about 950 TWh by 2030, around 3 percent of global electricity, with electricity supply for data centres growing past 1,000 TWh in 2030 in its Base Case and renewables meeting nearly half of the increase. The IEA, an intergovernmental energy agency, produced it to inform energy planning for artificial intelligence. Coverage: global with regional breakdowns (United States, China, Europe and others), annual from 2020 to 2035. Format and access: free online report chapters and charts with downloadable chart data on iea.org, under the IEA's terms, which allow reuse of much free material with attribution. Caveats: projections depend on scenario assumptions; site-level data are not published; iea.org blocks some automated readers. Simulation uses: demand scenarios for electricity system capacity planning, environmental impact studies of digital infrastructure, and stress tests of grids with data-centre clusters. Related records: the LBNL US report and the EU data-centre database give national and European figures.
